title: bisect-stash-replay-artifacts-notes
content:
Purpose: rapid personal breadcrumb for triage and a minimal playbook to bisect + pin artifacts when a canary shows degraded behaviour (503s / latency spikes).

Summary of incident (what I saw):
- Canary group for model-serving-1 started returning intermittent 503s around 2024-09-12 17:02 PDT after a routine release.
- Error rate climbed to ~6% for 95th percentile token latency, and the health check path (/healthz) returned 503 intermittently.
- Canary image tag: model-server:release-20240912-3 (floating tag in ECR).
- Canary had autoscaler spikes but CPU was modest; failures looked service-internal (SIGABRT OOM-ish stack traces in logs).

Quick reproduction steps I used: (local + cluster)
1) Fetch image digest we rolled:
   aws ecr describe-images --repository-name redwood/model-server --image-ids imageTag=release-20240912-3 --query 'imageDetails[0].imageDigest' --output text
   -> sha256:9f3b...b7

2) Pull locally to inspect layers:
   docker pull 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model-server@sha256:9f3b...
   docker inspect --format='{{json .Config.Labels}}' 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model-server@sha256:9f3b... | jq

3) Run minimal smoke locally (containerized):
   docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model-server@sha256:9f3b... \n     /bin/sh -c 'sleep 2 && curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" http://localhost:8080/healthz'

Observed output snippets I copied from canary pods:
- "2024-09-12T17:03:12Z [warn] kv-cache evicting stale entry for req 0x7f..."
- "fatal: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference (server.go:412)" followed by a minimal golang stack trace.
- kubelet logs: "container killed: OOMKilled" for 1/3 pods.

Notes on what I tried and why: (quick mental log)
- Tried kubectl rollout undo deploy/model-server --namespace serving-stage => NO-OP in our pipeline because we do image pinning by digest via the release controller; undo only rolled back ReplicaSet metadata but the controller reapplied digested image.
- Attempted immediate pin to previous digest I had in the manifest (release-20240905-2):
   kubectl set image deployment/model-server model-server=123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model-server@sha256:4a2c... --namespace serving-stage
   kubectl rollout status deploy/model-server --watch --namespace serving-stage
  Result: rollout succeeded, error rate dropped to <0.2% in 6m. Good fast mitigation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Regression in newly built model-server binary (compiler flags or a dependency) that causes memory corruption under certain prefix caching loads. (High prob: stacktrace + OOM)
2) New base image introduced glibc/allocator behaviour that changed memory footprint for mmap'ed KV cache. (Medium prob)
3) Artifact digest mismatch: manifest points at a different layer order that the runtime interprets incorrectly (low).

Bisect plan (how to find failing build quickly):
- We have daily artifacts and the pipeline embeds commit sha in image labels. Use image labels + git tag map to find candidate commits between 2024-09-05 (good) and 2024-09-12 (bad).
- Steps: pull labels, extract BUILD_COMMIT and BUILD_ID, then git bisect between those commits in the model-server repo.

Commands I ran for bisect prep: (save these)
- Get label: docker inspect --format='{{index .Config.Labels "build.commit"}}' <image>
- Map commit to PR: git show --name-only <commit> (look for changes to vector-kernel, allocator.c, alpine base)

If you need to run a proper bisection:
1) clone repo at commit range: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/model-server.git && cd model-server
2) git bisect start <bad-commit> <good-commit>
3) for each bisect step, build the image with local CI script and test smoke harness (fast):
   ./ci/build-image.sh --tag tmp-bisect --commit $COMMIT && docker run --rm tmp-bisect ./smoke-test.sh
   - smoke-test.sh hits /healthz and a few mocked inference paths, checks for memory leaks under short load (valgrind or malloc-stats if available)
4) mark good/bad and proceed.

Gotcha notes: our CI uses BUILD_ID that changes non-deterministically due to base layer caches — but binary artifacts include /bin/model-server with embedded version string. Prefer copying binary out of image and running it directly for deterministic local tests:
   docker create --name tmp 1234/...@sha256:9f3b... && docker cp tmp:/usr/local/bin/model-server ./model-server && docker rm tmp
   ./model-server --config test-config.yaml &>/tmp/ms.log & sleep 2; curl -s localhost:8080/healthz

Other useful checks (quick):
- Compare ldd of the binary across good/bad images: docker run --rm image ldd /usr/local/bin/model-server
- sha256sum of binary layers: docker save image | tar -xO layer.tar >/tmp/layer && sha256sum /tmp/layer
- Compare glibc versions: docker run --rm image ldd --version

Notes on pipelines and pinning strategy (longer term):
- Our release controller sometimes re-applies images based on tag; to avoid that we should always pin deployment manifests to digest on release and have the controller record an immutable release manifest in infra repo with image digests.
- Quick playbook to make a durable rollback PR (manual but fast):
  a) Create branch infra/rollback-pin-<timestamp>
  b) Update k8s/serving/deployments/model-server.yaml image: to the previous digest (4a2c...)
  c) Open PR against infra, add release notes, assign on-call release-engineer, trigger infra CI which applies change to serving-stage if approvals are green.

Debugging artifacts to collect if it happens again: (put these in an incident ticket)
- Pod logs (full) for 3 replicas (kubectl logs -p) and kubelet events.
- /proc/<pid>/maps and pmap output from within a running container (use nsenter if container dies quickly).
- Core dump (enable ulimit/core_pattern) and capture with gdb to get bt.
- Binary build metadata: BUILD_COMMIT, go build ldflags, CGO_ENABLED, base image digest.
- docker inspect labels for both good and bad.

Short checklist for on-call (1-pager):
- Isolate canary -> scale down canary weight (Argo Rollouts OR internal router)
- Pin to last-known-good digest with kubectl set image (command above)
- If that reduces error rate, open infra PR to pin permanently and mark release as reverted (BK ticket)
- If pin doesn't help, collect core/heap and escalate to Eng ML infra (Marco/Ellen)

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Are there any changes to jemalloc/allocator across base images between 2024-09-05 and 2024-09-12? (Ellen to check base image diffs)
- Can we add a cheap memory-sanity smoke test to our CI that runs a small kv-cache stress harness for 30s? (BK ticket created: BK-4382)
- Add automated manifest-digest snapshots to release controller logs for immediate rollbacks.

Random notes to self:
- Avoid relying on kubectl rollout undo — our controller is aggressive. Always set image by digest for immediate rollback.
- Keep one local copy of the last-good digest in personal notes (this file).

Raw commands history (copied from shell history)
- aws ecr describe-images --repository-name redwood/model-server --image-ids imageTag=release-20240912-3 --query 'imageDetails[0].imageDigest' --output text
- docker pull 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model-server@sha256:9f3b...
- docker create --name tmp 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model-server@sha256:9f3b...
- docker cp tmp:/usr/local/bin/model-server ./model-server
- kubectl set image deployment/model-server model-server=123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model-server@sha256:4a2c... --namespace serving-stage
- kubectl rollout status deploy/model-server --watch --namespace serving-stage\n
If you pick this up: start with the quick rollback command above; if it works, file infra PR and then follow the bisect plan to find the root cause. If you want me to run the initial bisection the next time I'm on-call, ping with a slot and I'll queue the Buildkite runs.

-- Aisha K. (personal scratchpad, keep ephemeral)
